table.name: account
table.purpose: Bank accounts: one row per account, with its home district, statement issuance frequency, and opening date (Czech bank data, labels in Czech).

col_001.name: account_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique account identifier. Referenced by transaction, order, credit card, loan, client and disposition tables.

col_002.name: district_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to the district lookup table (t05), which maps ids to Czech district names (e.g. 35 = Jablonec n. Nisou, 77 = Vsetin).

col_003.name: statement_issuance_frequency
col_003.description: Frequency of statement issuance: POPLATEK MESICNE = monthly, POPLATEK TYDNE = weekly, POPLATEK PO OBRATU = after each transaction.

col_004.name: account_opened_date
col_004.description: Date the account was opened, ranging from 1993-01-01 to 1997-12-29.

table.name: customers
table.purpose: Customer master table (one row per customer, 892 rows). Referenced by order/transaction tables (t01, t03, t05, t06). Holds a customer tier and an enrollment/registration date. Likely a bank or loyalty program (classic/junior/gold tiers).

col_001.name: customer_id
col_001.description: Primary key, surrogate customer identifier (1-1247, unique per row). Referenced by foreign keys in t01, t03, t05, t06.

col_002.name: account_number
col_002.description: Unique customer/account number (9-13660), one-to-one with keys in t03 and t04, so it identifies the same customer in those tables. Could be an external account number rather than a surrogate id.

col_003.name: customer_segment
col_003.description: Customer tier/segment: 'classic' (659), 'junior' (145), 'gold' (88). Suggests a banking or loyalty membership level.

col_004.name: enrollment_date
col_004.description: Customer since / account opening date, 1993-11-07 to 1998-12-29. Could alternatively be date of birth, but the range (all customers within ~5 years) fits a registration date better.

table.name: client
table.purpose: Persons/clients registry: one row per person with a unique ID, sex, birth date, and district (Czech district codes, e.g. Vyskov, Zdar nad Sazavou). Referenced by many other tables, so it is the central entity of the database.

col_001.name: person_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique person identifier. Referenced by many other tables (accounts, cards, loans, orders, etc.).

col_002.name: sex
col_002.description: Sex of the person: M = male, F = female.

col_003.name: birth_date
col_003.description: Date of birth (range 1911-1987, consistent with birth dates of adults).

col_004.name: district_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to district lookup table (t05), values 1-77 matching Czech districts (e.g. 63 = Vyskov, 66 = Zdar nad Sazavou). District where the person lives.

table.name: disposition
table.purpose: Links clients to bank accounts, specifying each client's role on the account (owner or authorized user/disponent). One row per client-account relationship. This matches the classic Berka/PKDD'99 Czech bank 'disp' table: 5369 rows, 4500 OWNER and 869 DISPONENT relationships, with a client_id referencing a clients table (t01) and an account_id referencing an accounts table (t03).

col_001.name: disp_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the disposition record; unique surrogate identifier for each client-account relationship.

col_003.name: client_id
col_003.description: Reference to the client (t01.col_001, clients table). 4500 distinct clients, each typically owning one account; some clients appear twice (owner of one account, disponent on another).

col_004.name: type
col_004.description: The client's role on the account: 'OWNER' (account holder, 4500 rows) or 'DISPONENT' (authorized disponent/user with access to the account, 869 rows).

table.name: districts_czechia
table.purpose: One row per Czech district (okres). 77 rows matches the 77 Czech districts (excluding Prague as separate? no, Prague included with ~1.2M). Columns hold district-level demographic and socio-economic indicators. Names like 'Brno - mesto', 'Havlickuv Brod', 'Jablonec n. Nisou' and regions like 'north Bohemia', 'south Moravia' confirm this is Czech district statistics (likely the well-known 'czechia' practice database).

col_001.name: district_id
col_001.description: Synthetic primary key, sequential 1-77, one per district.

col_002.name: district_name
col_002.description: Name of the Czech district (okres), e.g. 'Benesov', 'Brno - mesto', 'Jablonec n. Nisou'.

col_003.name: region
col_003.description: Name of the Czech region (kraj / historical region grouping) the district belongs to, e.g. 'south Moravia', 'central Bohemia', 'Prague'.

col_004.name: population
col_004.description: District population. Range 42,821 to 1,204,953; the maximum is Prague's population, and mid-values (~86k-139k) match typical Czech district sizes.

col_010.name: percentage_indicator
col_010.description: Float 33.9-100.0, looks like a percentage or index bounded by 100. Could be e.g. urbanization rate or a quality-of-life index; the exact quantity is not determinable.

col_011.name: average_salary
col_011.description: Values 8,110-12,541 CZK-like range with mean ~9,032; matches Czech district average monthly wage figures (in CZK hundreds, likely monthly gross wage). Prague highest.

col_012.name: unemployment_rate
col_012.description: Float 0.2-7.3 with a few nulls, typical of Czech district unemployment rates in percent. Alternative: some other small percentage rate.

col_013.name: crime_rate
col_013.description: Float 0.43-9.4, plausibly crimes per 1,000 inhabitants by district. Another small-rate indicator would also fit.

col_014.name: population_density
col_014.description: Integers 81-167; sample values (Jablonec 130, Havlickuv Brod 87, Vyskov 110) match typical Czech district population densities in inhabitants/km2. Alternative: some other bounded index.

col_015.name: business_entities_count
col_015.description: Counts 818-85,677 (max likely Prague). Plausibly number of self-employed persons or business entities in the district; exact entity type unresolved.

col_016.name: companies_count
col_016.description: Counts 888-99,107, closely tracking col_015 per row. Plausibly number of companies/legal entities in the district; exact entity type unresolved.

table.name: loan
table.purpose: Loan accounts: one row per loan with origination date, principal amount, term in months, monthly payment, and a letter grade (likely credit/risk grade). col_002 links each loan one-to-one to a customer record in t01.

col_001.name: loan_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the loan record.

col_002.name: customer_id
col_002.description: Reference to t01.col_001 (one-to-one), identifying the customer/borrower associated with this loan.

col_003.name: origination_date
col_003.description: Date the loan was opened/originated, ranging 1993-07-05 to 1998-12-08.

col_004.name: loan_amount
col_004.description: Principal amount of the loan, apparently in cents (values 4,980 to 590,820, i.e. ~$49.80 to ~$5,908.20). Consistent with col_006 monthly payment and col_005 term: e.g. 76080 cents / 12 months ≈ 6340 cents payment.

col_005.name: term_months
col_005.description: Loan term in months; only values 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 occur. Also matches lookup tables t02/t03/t04 (likely term lookup tables).

col_006.name: monthly_payment
col_006.description: Scheduled monthly payment amount in cents (304 to 9,910, i.e. ~$3.04 to ~$99.10); roughly loan_amount / term_months in the sample rows.

col_007.name: grade
col_007.description: Single-letter grade A, B, C, D (C most common, then A, D, B). Most plausibly a credit/risk grade of the loan; the specific code meanings are not independently confirmed, so an alternative categorical code cannot be fully excluded.

table.name: orders
table.purpose: Permanent/standing payment orders (the classic Berka Czech bank dataset 'order' table): each row is a recurring payment order from a bank account to a recipient account, with amount and payment type symbol.

col_001.name: order_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the payment order; unique sequential integer.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning bank account the order is charged to; references the accounts table (t01.col_001), many orders per account.

col_003.name: recipient_bank_code
col_003.description: Two-letter code of the recipient bank (13 distinct banks, roughly uniform). Opaque anonymized bank codes.

col_004.name: recipient_account_number
col_004.description: Account number of the payment recipient; nearly unique per row, large numeric values consistent with anonymized account numbers.

col_005.name: amount
col_005.description: Payment amount, presumably in Czech koruna (CZK); ranges 1 to 14,882, median ~2,596.

col_006.name: payment_symbol
col_006.description: Czech payment type symbol (k_symbol): SIPO = household/utility payment, POJISTNE = insurance, UVER = loan repayment, LEASING = leasing payment; empty string = unspecified/other.

table.name: trans
table.purpose: Bank account transactions (Czech bank dataset): one row per transaction on an account, with date, type, operation, balance after transaction, amount, and characterization codes.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the account the transaction belongs to; references t01.col_001 (accounts). 4500 distinct accounts.

col_004.name: type
col_004.description: Transaction type in Czech: PRIJEM = credit/income, VYDAJ = debit/expense, VYBER = cash withdrawal.

col_005.name: operation
col_005.description: Transaction operation mode in Czech: VYBER = cash withdrawal, VKLAD = cash deposit, PREVOD NA UCET = transfer to another account, PREVOD Z UCTU = transfer from another account, VYBER KARTOU = card withdrawal. Null when type is VYBER (redundant).

col_006.name: balance
col_006.description: Account balance after the transaction, in Czech koruna (CZK).

col_007.name: amount
col_007.description: Transaction amount in CZK; can be negative (min -41126), likely for reversals/fees.

col_008.name: k_symbol
col_008.description: Characterization of the transaction in Czech: UROK = interest credited, SLUZBY = services/payment for statement, SIPO = household payments, DUCHOD = pension, SANKC. UROK = sanction interest, POJISTNE = insurance, UVER = loan payment, etc. Blank/null when not applicable.

col_009.name: bank
col_009.description: Code of the other bank in inter-bank transfers (two-letter codes); null for non-transfer transactions.

col_010.name: account
col_010.description: Account number at the other bank for inter-bank transfers; null for non-transfer transactions. 0 appears as a placeholder.
